elements.quote: Prior reviews of conversion therapy in HCC have mainly addressed whether initially unresectable tumors can be downstaged to resection, focusing on tumor response, conversion-tosurgery rate, resection rate, safety, and perioperative outcomes [5,6]. Less attention has been given to the subsequent clinical decision faced after successful downstaging: whether proceeding to hepatectomy adds survival benefit beyond the prognosis already conferred by treatment response, preserved liver function, and favorable tumor biology. The present review addresses this distinction by focusing on comparative survival after conversion or salvage hepatectomy.

elements.quote: In clinical practice, patients who proceed to hepatectomy are usually those with sustained disease control, adequate liver-function reserve, preserved performance status, controlled or absent extrahepatic disease, and technically resectable lesions [36]. These factors are themselves prognostic and may partly explain the survival differences between surgical and non-surgical groups. Accordingly, the pooled HRs are best understood as reflecting survival within a selected post-conversion surgical pathway rather than a pure surgical treatment effect. ... hepatectomy should be considered for carefully selected patients after effective downstaging
